findings.title: Alert page still scrolls sideways at every phone width when the local AI is unavailable (the fix does not cover it; same in the original)
findings.repro: Fixed AHM-03 build, Ollama not running (the guide's default). Upload tests/fixtures/zeek/telnet as a zip, then open /alerts/<telnet id> in Analyst mode at 320, 360, 375, 390 or 414 px with any font.
findings.evidence: 25/25 combos sideways. scrollWidth is 454 (default and Noto Sans), 488 (DejaVu Sans), 438 (Liberation Sans) and 435 (Roboto) at every width, so scrollX is 79 at 375 px. Cause: the div.banner text 'local AI not reachable at http://127.0.0.1:11434: HTTPConnectionPool(host='127.0.0.1', ... (Caused by NewConnectionError("HTTPConnection(host='127.0.0.1', port=11434): ...' contains an unbreakable token. That text runs to x=454 while the banner box ends at 304 px (320 viewport) or 398 px (414 viewport). It also makes axe report color-contrast 'incomplete' on .banner at 375 px. Original build: identical numbers. Screenshots: shots/fixed-AHM-03-alert-banner-375-scrolled-right.png and shots/fixed-AHM-03-alert-analyst-375-full.png (454 px wide).
findings.fix: Add `.banner { overflow-wrap: anywhere; }` to app.css. Verified through CSSOM: 0/25 combos sideways and the axe incomplete disappears. Optionally also shorten the reason text in maxguard/ai/ollama_client.py (Jonattan's module).

findings.title: Test method: page.addStyleTag cannot inject the test fonts because the dashboard's CSP refuses inline styles
findings.repro: On any dashboard page call page.addStyleTag({content: 'html, body, input, button, select, label { font-family: "Liberation Sans" !important }'}).
findings.evidence: It throws 'page.addStyleTag: Refused to apply inline style because it violates the following Content Security Policy directive: "style-src 'self'"' and logs a console error. getComputedStyle(body).fontFamily stays 'system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif', so a sweep built this way silently measures only the default font.
findings.fix: In the guide or test, inject the font with CSSOM, which the CSP allows: `const s=new CSSStyleSheet(); s.replaceSync('html, body, input, button, select, label, .stack td::before { font-family: "Liberation Sans" !important }'); document.adoptedStyleSheets=[...document.adoptedStyleSheets, s];`. Confirmed: the computed font changed in 140/140 measurements per font.

== Method notes ==
1) page.addStyleTag is blocked by the CSP (see F-5); fonts were injected with a constructed stylesheet and confirmed in 140 measurements per font.
2) Playwright element screenshots add style="" to inputs. On the next swap htmx copies that attribute, and the CSP logs 'Refused to apply inline style' (source htmx-2.0.11.min.js). With keyboard or click only: 0 errors. Take screenshots after the interactions.
3) The first parallel F4 run on the original builds was discarded: both servers got SIGTERM from outside my scripts mid-run ('Shutting down' in the logs). Re-running each in its own session (setsid) completed.
4) On the originals, page.evaluate on a tab whose navigation never finished hangs forever; calls are now bounded at 1.5 s.

findings.title: Non-holder queue tabs no longer catch up when they load: Back after Upload or Save shows stale alerts for up to 30 s (regression)
findings.repro: cd /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-maxguard/d28fe4b6-2c9f-5cd0-8e7f-d2be65aa4c01/scratchpad/agentwork/fix-review/scripts && node t5_back_stale.js orig-03 fixed-03 && node t5_back_stale.js bfcache orig-03 fixed-03 && node t15_upload_back.js orig-02 fixed-02 && UPLOADER=holder node t15_upload_back.js orig-02 fixed-02. Flow: open two queue tabs. In one tab, open an alert, set Investigating, Save, press Back. Or: go to Upload, upload, press Back.
findings.evidence: The server sends alerts-changed once on connect so a page that may have missed a change refreshes (app.py alert_events). In the original every tab had its own stream and got that event. In the fix only the lock holder gets it. Back loads the queue from the HTTP cache (transferSize 0), so the page is old and nothing refreshes it until the 30 s poll. t5 fixed-03: "queueShowsRightAfterBack":"New","queueShowsInvestigating":"NO, still \"New\" 8110 ms after Back" (bfcache on: 8153 ms); orig-03: "after 64 ms". t15 fixed-02: "still 1 row(s) 8147 ms after Back (server has 2)"; orig-02 "2 rows after 80 ms". The same happens when the uploading tab was the holder, because it loses the lock when it leaves: "still 1 row(s) 8131 ms". A new non-holder tab also misses any change made between the server rendering it and DOMContentLoaded.

findings.title: A queue page in the back/forward cache gets the lock but cannot run, so no tab opens the stream (regression)
findings.repro: node t6_bfcache_pending.js orig-03 fixed-03 (full Chromium, bfcache on, as in normal Chrome); WAIT_S=90 node t6_bfcache_pending.js fixed-03. Flow: queue tabs H (holder) and N. N goes to Upload (its queue page enters bfcache with its lock request pending). Close H, open a new queue tab X, change an alert.
findings.evidence: Chrome 141 gives the lock to N's page while it is in bfcache, and the callback only runs when N is restored. fixed-03: "streams":"H","locksFromX":"held=1 pending=1","newTabLiveRefresh":"NO after 5002 ms (rows 1, server 2)". With WAIT_S=90 the lock is still held and there is still no stream after 95 s. Only when N comes Back does "streamsEnd" become "H,N". orig-03: "streams":"H,N,X","newTabLiveRefresh":"yes 479 ms". Until Chrome evicts that page (its bfcache lifetime) every queue tab is limited to the 30 s poll. A holder never enters bfcache (notRestoredReasons "lock"), so only waiting pages are affected.

findings.title: When the holder's stream is answered with an HTTP error, that tab keeps the lock with a dead stream and blocks every other tab (regression, needs a reverse proxy)
findings.repro: node t7_stream_502.js orig-03 fixed-03. The server stops, a stub answers 502 on the same port (as nginx does while its upstream restarts), the server comes back, then a new queue tab is opened and an alert changes.
findings.evidence: EventSource stops reconnecting for good after a non-200 answer. The fixed holder still holds the lock, so no tab ever opens a new stream. fixed-03: "streamsAfterNewTab":"H,H","liveRefresh":{"newTabX":"NO within 5 s","oldTabH":"NO"}. orig-03: "streamsAfterNewTab":"H,H,X","newTabX":"yes 381 ms". Without a proxy (connection refused) EventSource keeps retrying and recovers (t13 part d passes). ARCHITECTURE.md describes running behind a reverse proxy, and app.py sets X-Accel-Buffering for nginx.

result.measurements:
I tested the fixed AHM-02/03/ALL builds against the originals, from private copies in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-maxguard/d28fe4b6-2c9f-5cd0-8e7f-d2be65aa4c01/scratchpad/agentwork/fix-review. Browser: Playwright 1.56.1, Chromium 141.0.7390.37. Playwright launches Chromium with bfcache turned off, and the headless shell never restores pages from it ('masked' even for static pages). So every bfcache result comes from a run with channel 'chromium' and ignoreDefaultArgs ['--disable-back-forward-cache']; there a static page is restored. Firefox and WebKit are not installed, and nothing was installed for this review. The full Chromium build tried to reach Google update hosts; the proxy refused them, and the MaxGuard pages made no outside requests.

Verdict: the template, title, focus-id and CSS parts of the fix are sound. The tests are C3-C9 and C14-C17 in the checks list: focus stays on the same link or button with :focus-visible, ids are unique hex, the title is escaped and falls back correctly, and the CSS has no side effects at 1280/375/320 px in five fonts. The Web Locks + BroadcastChannel design fixes the six-connection problem (the original's 7th tab never loads; the fixed one loads in 69 ms). It also handles closing the holder, a holder crash, two origins (one stream per origin), a plain server restart and CDP-frozen tabs, with exactly one refresh per tab per change. It has three regressions:
- F1 (high): pages from Back or the HTTP cache stay stale for up to 30 s with 2 or more queue tabs, because only the holder gets the server's first event.
- F2 (medium): a page waiting for the lock is granted it while in bfcache.
- F3 (low): a holder whose stream got a proxy 502 never lets go of the lock.
F4 (low, pre-existing): htmx drops a refresh asked for mid-request or while the table settles.

Combined patch (F1-F4), tested: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-maxguard/d28fe4b6-2c9f-5cd0-8e7f-d2be65aa4c01/scratchpad/agentwork/fix-review/patched-03/maxguard/web/static/app.js, as a diff in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-maxguard/d28fe4b6-2c9f-5cd0-8e7f-d2be65aa4c01/scratchpad/agentwork/fix-review/patch-app.js.diff. Every failing scenario passes with it, the earlier checks still pass, and pytest gives 18 / 39 / 54 passed. The same app.js serves AHM-02, AHM-03 and ALL.

Notes, not defects:
- (a) The fixed holder page is never kept in bfcache (notRestoredReasons 'lock'). Back reloads it and it is correct.
- (b) On a plain-http LAN address navigator.locks is missing (isSecureContext false), so the fallback opens one stream per tab. The app.js comment 'Older browsers' should also name that case.
- (c) If F1-F3 are taken, update the live-refresh prose in fix/docgen/plan_ahmad.py lines 111-117. The roadmap docs embed app.js through @@FILE, so regenerating them picks up the code.
